now: v1.4.0 — SKY AND WORLD REFINED. Detailed clouds and cirrus, physical night lighting, finer ocean waves and terrain relief, with the rebuilt aircraft integrated into the curved world.
ledger: 2026-09-24 v1.4.0 — Clouds, sky and landscapes rebuilt through repeated visual refinement. Full-resolution cloud lighting, 8K cirrus, catalogued stars and mapped Moon, 512² fine water, real 5 m central Valdez elevation data, near terrain and snow detail. Aircraft coating and self-shadows share the world lighting.

2026-09-24 v1.3.0 — Aircraft graphics rebuilt and refined through five further passes. New cockpit and mechanical detail, paint and engine materials, articulated bays, volumetric exhaust, and shared distance/quality levels. Browser checks pass on WebGPU and WebGL; combat simulation remains unchanged.

2026-09-24 v1.2.0: Flight and combat audio rebuilt. Recorded afterburner texture, spool-driven turbine detail, round-aligned cannon attacks, moving aircraft and missiles, delayed blasts, gear and ground-contact sounds, and distinct threat tones. Audition the mix in the audio lab.

2026-08-10 v1.0.0 — SHIPPED. Four days ago this was an empty repository and one sentence: rebuild War Thunder with one plane, playable in my browser. Today it is an F-22 over three real places on Earth — thirty authored sorties, a persistent war, aces with grudges, dogfights with honest physics, a radio that never lies and can now speak, installable, accessible, and verified by seven hundred thirty-nine automated gates that all run green. One plane. Three fronts. No install. Fly it.

2026-08-09 v0.36.2 — INSTALLABLE: RAPTOR is a PWA now — install it from the browser and it opens fullscreen, landscape, with its own icon. The service worker keeps only the tiny shell offline-capable; the terrain stays streamed (nobody wants a 400MB install).
2026-08-09 v0.36.1 — the mixer's last channel: WEAPONS VOLUME. The cannon gets its own fader (some pilots want the M61 to rattle the desk; some want to hear the radio over it).

2026-08-09 v0.36.0 — THE VOICE (experimental): flip RADIO VOICE in settings and the war talks — OVERLORD gets a measured British calm, enemy aces get a low deliberate menace (an ace is never hurried — urgent calls speed up for everyone else, never for them), and your own pilot answers in kind. All 410 radio lines cast automatically. Ships OFF by default: it's built on the voices your machine already has, and honesty about that is the feature.

2026-08-09 — SCOPE CUT (Chris): multiplayer is out — no P2P duels, no server battles. RAPTOR ships v1.0 as a complete single-pilot war: the campaign, the operation, the aces. The determinism foundation stays (it's what makes replays and the hash-gated QA possible), but nobody's building netcode.

2026-08-09 v0.35.1 — polish riders: VIPER's escape chase now announces itself in its window, TYPHOON's objective reads NO ESCAPE on the HUD, M10's turn line is true on every path, JACKAL's dawn geometry corrected, V10's clock honest to the second. The finale panel's top five, all in.

2026-08-09 v0.35.0 — THE FINALE: the campaign is complete. Thirty authored sorties across three real fronts, ending in three campaign closers — PAID IN FULL (everything NELLIS taught you converges while JACKAL's ledger closes), THE HOMECOMING (defend the fleet you escorted in sortie three, by the same lamp), and TYPHOON: the last boss over the sinking flagship, the campaign's only mandatory ace kill — let him reach the fence and the war ends unfinished. Victory cards now speak: OVERLORD's actual closing words replace the generic banner on every mission. Four drama panels reviewed all thirty; the radio never lied once.

2026-08-09 v0.34.0 — TWENTY-FOUR DEEP: the tightening third. BIG FRIENDS (escort friendly heavies through an enemy intercept — check fire around the package), FUMES (a dawn raid answered by the campaign's first non-ace tier-4s), THE BELT (VALDEZ's first spawned SAM belt), SECOND WIND (BOREAS comes back for you — if the wind still has hands), THE EYE (a guarded high-value orbiter), and TWO DOORS (hold two intercept doors at once, each with a gun waiting on the lane). Third drama panel signed off; the radio still never lies. Six sorties remain — and TYPHOON.

2026-08-09 v0.33.0 — EIGHTEEN DEEP: the campaign's escalating middle third. THE AIR BRIDGE (strangle an airlift before wheels-down), THE COUNTERPUSH (for once the ground wins the war — you just keep JACKAL off their backs), STILL WATER (a silent midnight-sun harbor raid), HOLD UNTIL RELIEVED (a station-defense marathon with three relays and a coda), SCATTER (SEAD, then chase the survivors down two roads), and FOUR CORNERS — the campaign's first honest 4-v-1. A second drama panel reviewed every beat; its fixes are in, including radio that never lies about the clock.

2026-08-08 v0.32.0 — YOUR COCKPIT, YOUR RULES: a real settings menu inside Esc — graphics quality with honest live/reload labels, render scale and field-of-view sliders that apply instantly, a three-channel audio mixer, motion reduction for flash-sensitive pilots, subtitle scaling, and colorblind-safe HUD marker palettes (deuteranopia/tritanopia). Auto quality still benchmarks your machine on first run; now you can overrule it.

2026-08-08 v0.31.0 — TWELVE SORTIES DEEP: the authored campaign doubles — six new set-pieces including night convoy work and friendly escort duty, plus every fix the drama panel ordered on the first six. Contacts now EARN their HUD diamond: you see a bandit when it closes inside 18km or turns against you, so when OVERLORD calls a pop-up group, it actually pops up.

2026-08-08 v0.30.0 — THE CAMPAIGN OPENS: six authored sorties, two per front, each built on a seven-beat arc — briefing, ingress radio, the objective, THE TURN (an authored ambush that arrives exactly when it should), climax, resolution. FIRST BLOOD over Nevada, JACKAL'S HOUR against a live SAM ring, HOLD THE NARROWS in the fjords, a drone footrace to the fence, the reef line, and THE HORNET'S NEST with SHRIKE waiting in the haze. Linear unlock chain in the hangar; a three-judge drama panel reviewed every beat and its fixes are in. The autoplay harness that proves every sortie winnable AND losable is now the permanent content gate.

2026-08-08 v0.29.0 — THE NEMESIS: the war has names now. Aces fly with red-marked jets and a star on your HUD. Your first Sidewinder leaves one smoking, not dead — and a smart ace firewalls the throttle and runs for the map edge trailing black smoke. Let him cross and the hangar remembers: NEMESIS ALIVE. He comes back in later sorties, better than before, with a grudge and a radio voice. Kill him before the fence and his name comes off their board for good.

2026-08-08 v0.28.0 — THE SKY SHOOTS BACK: the first real dogfights. Fighters see you, turn in, and shoot — their missiles trip your MISSILE warning before they can hurt you, their guns only bite inside 700m, and they jink your Sidewinders off bad shots exactly like you dodge theirs. Energy is honest both ways: a bandit that turns too hard goes slow, breaks off to rebuild speed, then comes back. INTERCEPT and CAP sorties now appear in the campaign — the deeper you push the front, the harder the sky fights back.

2026-08-08 v0.27.0 — THE FIRST BANDITS: enemy aircraft exist. Drones, transports and fighters fly waypoint routes with honest physics (energy bleed in hard turns, terrain-following floor), raiders dive on your convoys and shoot back at ships, and your AIM-9X finally leads a MOVING target — the guidance law that misses a 150 m/s crosser by 8 meters now kills it at 2.8. Dashed diamonds track every contact. Plus: cloud shadows reach the sea, and the valdez camera-ring artifact is root-caused and gone.
2026-08-08 v0.26.0 — THE LONG WAR — persistent operations: generated sorties push a real front line (win +2km toward victory at +16), the hangar remembers your war, deterministic 200-sortie chains
2026-08-08 v0.25.0 — THE LIVING BATTLEFIELD — 48-unit war: driving convoys, mid-sortie reinforcements, friendly forces, rearm pads on all three fronts
2026-08-08 v0.24.0 — THE FIRST SORTIE — mission system: objectives HUD, radio comms, STRIKE + SEAD sorties over Nevada (?mission=), deterministic replays
2026-08-08 v0.23.0 — SHADOWS OF THE WAR — cloud shadows now cast by the real volumetric cloud field (dappled desert, tower shadows on the reef)
2026-08-08 v0.22.0 — THE HANGAR DOOR — death/victory kill cam (4s crash orbit, HUD fades), pre-flight hangar: front cards + time-of-day presets + FLY

2026-08-07 v0.21.0 — EYES THAT ADAPT: the camera now meters the scene like a human eye — quick to brighten into shadowed fjords, slow to recover from glare. The golden-hour shots across all three fronts finally sit within two-thirds of a stop of each other (the last big 'ships imperfect' item, now closed).

2026-08-07 v0.20.0 — THE WAR HAS RULES: tickets on both sides, three lives, an airfield that rearms you if you come in low and slow, a battle boundary that warns then bites, and a VICTORY screen you have to earn by breaking the whole ground war. The sandbox is now a game you can win or lose.

2026-08-07 v0.19.0 — PASS THREE, mandate complete: three judge panels, 22 measured fixes, and a final ship-readiness scorecard. The last pass caught its own subtleties (a cloud shadow anchor 'interpolating a crossing that never existed', a glint comb that WAS the fix for the previous problem) and closed with an honest list of conscious imperfections. The three 10%-better passes are done.

2026-08-07 v0.18.0 — PASS TWO: the second judge panel widened every measurement and caught two of our own pass-1 fixes only holding where we'd measured them — both re-fixed globally (including under camera motion). Plus: combat finally LOOKS like combat (muzzle flash, hot tracers, impact sparks), the ocean lost its denim moire, and the golden-hour fjord mirrors the orange sky.

2026-08-07 v0.17.0 — PASS ONE: a six-judge panel tore the game apart frame by frame and all 8 findings got fixed with measurements: cloud dot-lattice root-caused to a shadow term (10x cleaner), Nevada's air un-blued, the sun disc warms at sunset, HUD readable against clouds, living water with real glints, organic coastlines, and the phase-1 scale pylons finally retired from the ocean.
2026-08-07 v0.16.2 — THROTTLE, PERFECTED (per Chris): hold W to 100%, keep holding for afterburner, let go and it settles at 100% — exactly like War Thunder. Mouse never touches the throttle.

2026-08-07 v0.16.1 — NEW AIRFRAME: the F-22 rebuilt at 4x the detail — smooth blended fuselage, real chines, gold bubble canopy, thrust-vectoring nozzles. The builder critiqued its own screenshots through six rounds before showing it.

2026-08-07 v0.16.0 — REAL SKIES: the clouds are volumes now — the GPU marches rays through 3D cloud fields with real light scattering. Towering Pacific cumulus, Alaska overcast decks, Nevada fair-weather puffs — and you can fly through them. Still 121fps.

2026-08-07 v0.15.0 — SAM CITY: the missile sites launch back. Launch warning tone + flashing MISSILE alert, then physics decides: fly straight and it connects; turn away on the warning and run, and it dies chasing you. Every counter-tactic works because the physics is real, not scripted.

2026-08-07 v0.14.0 — FOX TWO: AIM-9X Sidewinders. The seeker locks onto targets (box + growl tone), the missile launches with real rocket physics — boost, sustain, burnout — and steers itself in with the same guidance law real missiles use. First test flight missed forever because one minus sign was flipped; the test caught it.

2026-08-07 v0.13.0 — THE SEA COMPUTES: the ocean is now a real physics simulation running on your GPU — thousands of waves computed 120 times a second (verified against textbook math to 14 decimal places), with foam that forms where waves actually break. Alaska chop and Pacific swell are physically different seas now. Plus: ground units render 6x leaner.

2026-08-07 v0.12.0 — THE AIR IS REAL: the sky is now computed from actual atmospheric physics — light scattered by real air molecules. Distant mountains fade into blue with distance, sunsets ignite a true twilight arch, all verified against a physics reference to 8 decimal places. 90/90 tests.

2026-08-07 v0.11.0 — THE WAR SHOOTS BACK: anti-aircraft guns track you and fire leaded bursts (red tracers). Hull damage, red-flash hits, shot down = respawn. Nevada's real satellite imagery also landed — all three fronts are photographic now. 65/65 tests.

2026-08-07 v0.10.0 — THE REAL EARTH: actual aerial photography draped over Alaska and the Marianas (sub-meter USGS source), plus laser-scan normal maps and baked ambient shadows on all three fronts. The fjords look like the real fjords now.
2026-08-07 v0.9.0 — THE AAA PASS BEGINS: rebuilt render pipeline — temporal anti-aliasing, HDR bloom (sun halo + water-glint sparkle), lens ghosts. 121fps with it all on. 51/51 tests.

2026-08-07 THE MANDATE — new goal: the most beautiful game possible in a browser, built for the most powerful Macs. An 8-agent research fleet mapped the ceiling; the AAA rebuild starts now, then three full 10%-better passes.

2026-08-07 v0.8.0 — TARGETS ON THE GROUND: 29 units across the three fronts (convoy + SAM site in Nevada, ships in the Alaska Sound, a carrier group off Saipan). Shoot them, they burn. Kills score on screen.

2026-08-07 v0.7.0 — THE GUN WORKS: 6000-rounds-a-minute cannon with honest ballistics (bullets slow down and drop like real ones), glowing tracers, dust where they hit the desert, engine + gun sound. 11/11 tests.
2026-08-06 v0.6.0 — YOU FLY: mouse steers the jet, W/S throttle, real physics, crash and respawn. The game became a game.
2026-08-06 v0.5.0 — the sea is real: waves that match each place — glassy fjords in Alaska, Pacific swell over the reef.
2026-08-06 v0.4.0 — the ground is real: actual US Geological Survey elevation data for Nevada, Alaska and the Marianas. Zero seams, verified by pixel measurement.
2026-08-06 v0.3.0 — a sky that knows the time: physically-computed daylight, the sun where it really is, stars at night.
2026-08-06 v0.1.0 — the engine boots: runs in any browser, simulation so precise two computers get identical results.
2026-08-06 day zero — plan approved: 21 phases, one F-22, three real battlefields.
